Bug_Title: EC: Call to equals() comparing unrelated class and interface (EC_UNRELATED_CLASS_AND_INTERFACE)
Bug_Details:
This method calls equals(Object) on two references,  one of which is a class
and the other an interface, where neither the class nor any of its
non-abstract subclasses implement the interface.
Therefore, the objects being compared
are unlikely to be members of the same class at runtime
(unless some application classes were not analyzed, or dynamic class
loading can occur at runtime).
According to the contract of equals(),
objects of different
classes should always compare as unequal; therefore, according to the
contract defined by java.lang.Object.equals(Object),
the result of this comparison will always be false at runtime.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is demonstrated by calling equals() on two references, one of which is a String (class) and the other is a Comparable<Integer> (interface). Neither the class nor any of its non-abstract subclasses implement the Comparable<Integer> interface, hence they are unrelated. According to the contract of equals(), objects of different classes should always compare as unequal, making this comparison always false.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUnit test calls the method showBug() from the UnrelatedEquals class, which contains a bug where equals() is used to compare a String object with a Comparable<Integer> object. These two are unrelated, and the contract of equals() dictates that objects of different classes should always compare as unequal. Therefore, this test is set to assertTrue, expecting true, but it will always return false, thus making the test fail and triggering the bug.
